readerQuestion: How can Home Assistant dim a lamp when my TV starts playing, raise it on pause, and stop changing the room when the household does not want movie lighting?
directAnswer: First observe the actual media-player states in every intended app. Use a visible TV lighting allowed toggle and a five-second cancellable settling delay, rehearse with persistent notifications, then connect one dimmable nonessential lamp. Android TV Remote alone does not report playback status; unreliable app states require a different source or manual lighting. The example uses fixed 15/45/65 percent levels rather than restoring a previous setting.
originalContribution: Sections #observe, #preview and #rehearsal combine a playback-source decision table with complete preview YAML and a six-row household rehearsal. Section #lamp gives the exact action replacement after validation. Sixteen isolated Home Assistant Core 2026.10.1 checks exercised the published logic using simulated entities and recorded service calls: five main cases retained the original five-second delay, and the remaining state/action matrix used a 100ms delay only to shorten the checks. No hardware was connected. This verifies opt-in while already playing, quick-resume cancellation, deliberate pause, off-during-wait cancellation, ignored buffering/unknown/unavailable/on, recognized states, attribute-only suppression, fixed notification ID and numeric brightness targeting.
limitations: Documentation research and isolated runtime checks do not establish physical TV, app or lamp compatibility, actual response latency, or installed-version UI availability. App state accuracy must be observed in the reader's home. Fixed brightness does not restore earlier lighting; permission must be turned off after watching. Older toggle-helper versions may restore previous permission after restart if the current startup option is absent. The generated cover illustrates a room and is not installation evidence. No human or expert review is claimed.
proofreadFixes: Final automated plain-English review added explicit horizontal-scroll guidance beside the long YAML and the second table after mobile inspection. Updated the method note to describe the completed isolated Home Assistant checks and explicitly exclude physical-device testing. Verified that permission checks inside actions allow an off event to cancel the pending delay; moving that check to top-level conditions would change cancellation behavior. Confirmed that on/unknown/unavailable/buffering send no command, a recovered recognized state may run again when allowed, and Run actions does not prove the trigger. Confirmed the final light.turn_on step can illuminate an off lamp and that 65% is a fixed finish level. Retained the visible caveats rather than promising automatic previous-state restoration, movie detection, guaranteed timing or universal app support.

claimChecks.claim: Media-player on means playback details are not known; playing, paused, idle, buffering, unavailable and unknown are distinct states. A power-only signal cannot drive a reliable play/pause rule.

Android TV Remote supplies remote/power control but not playback status. Google Cast can report supported app content; it also has power-state and app-support limits, so combining entries cannot invent missing information.
A state trigger with to:null excludes attribute-only updates. The isolated Core check confirmed a media_position-only update did not start this example.

Restart mode cancels the earlier running sequence when a new eligible trigger arrives. Top-level conditions remain empty and permission is checked inside actions, allowing permission-off to cancel the waiting run. Already executed commands are not undone.

Toggle helpers normally restore previous state. Current documentation exposes More options / Each time Home Assistant starts / Turn off; changing this option does not change the current state. Article qualifies UI availability by installed version.
persistent_notification.create is an in-frontend preview, and a fixed notification_id overwrites that notification. The example sends no lamp command before the explicit replacement step.

light.turn_on with brightness_pct requests a percentage and can turn on an off lamp. The isolated replacement-action check recorded integer 15 and only light.tv_lamp as target; physical brightness was not measured.

Run actions skips the real trigger and top-level condition evaluation, while condition steps inside actions still apply. The article requires actual remote-driven state changes for trigger verification.
Reading States is harmless; editing a state does not control the underlying device but can trigger real automations. Readers are instructed to observe States and operate their normal remote.
